<reason>Both sides argued the motion as written and both openings were clipped, so that execution cost cancels. PRO built the cleaner decision frame early — judge on whether the next generation ever encounters the institution, and note that the motion only moves the marginal pound — and then defended it consistently: "sovereignty was always rented" answered CON's tenancy/data point plausibly, and Q1 (how does a seventeen-year-old discover a newly launched channel?) exposed the load-bearing gap in CON's case. CON's answer to that question was resourceful but costly: it redefined channel expansion as owned apps, strands inside iPlayer, prominence, and "trailers on platforms," which PRO fairly crystallised as "my motion wearing a coat" — an admission that feed-facing discovery is the gating step. PRO's closing risk asymmetry (destinations still stand and clips point at them, versus a fully commissioned service with no route in) gave the reader a clean tiebreaker. CON landed real damage: the Attenborough distinction (trust travelled through an employed, edited face inside the house) was the sharpest single hit of the debate, and "the marginal pound is the hour" punished PRO's loose "you can always commission another hour." But CON's decisive counter — that the destination is static and youth arrive at "a shelf commissioned for over-50s" — rests on an unsupported assertion about existing catalogues, and it half-concedes PRO's premise by proposing new youth commissioning plus clip marketing. PRO's route to victory survived the exchange more intact; CON's required an empirical claim it never grounded.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Q1 and its follow-through: asking how a seventeen-year-old discovers a newly launched channel forced CON to answer with owned apps and "trailers on platforms," which PRO then converted in closing into "that is my motion wearing a coat" — accepting feed-based discovery as the gating step. CON's best counterpunch (Attenborough was employed and edited inside the house, and "some audience follows the face" concedes rented attention) was damaging but narrower in scope.</best_rebuttal>
